Measured: campaign PBO 0.6159 (gate <=0.50), campaign White RC p 0.4220 (gate <0.05) -> every candidate vetoed regardless of individual merit. The genuinely per-candidate gates DO discriminate (walk_forward 58.1%, fragility 47.9%, cpcv 43.3%, capacity 43.3%, expected_value 40.2%) and sole-cause failures is EMPTY, so no gate is uniquely killing good candidates today. THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM: campaign PBO rises with generation volume, so a large mostly-noise campaign mechanically vetoes a genuinely good candidate submitted alongside it -- which CONTRADICTS the desk's own TWO_STAGE_DISCOVERY_LAW ('generation volume is unbounded and can never create a phantom edge there'; 'the confirmation bar never rises with generation'). NOT FIXED AUTONOMOUSLY: any change here relaxes validation-gate strictness, which constitution point 5 forbids the cycle from touching. Needs a principal/panel ruling on whether the screen should RANK on campaign PBO/RC (per the law) rather than VETO on them.
